title: Two-step max over child RSS samples and resource peak is partially redundant
description: The child peak is computed as `child_peak_rss = max(child_rss_samples, default=child_resource_peak)` followed by a conditional `child_peak_rss = max(child_peak_rss, child_resource_peak)`. When `child_rss_samples` is empty, the `default=child_resource_peak` already sets `child_peak_rss` to `child_resource_peak`, and the subsequent `max(child_resource_peak, child_resource_peak)` is a no-op. When samples are non-empty, the second line does the real combine. The intent (overall max of all polled samples plus the resource-reported peak, or None if nothing is available) is expressible as a single filtered aggregation, e.g. `candidates = [*child_rss_samples]; if child_resource_peak is not None: candidates.append(child_resource_peak); child_peak_rss = max(candidates, default=None)`. The current form relies on the `default=` value overlapping the second `max` operand, which is non-obvious and easy to misread as a bug.
evidence: Lines 259-261. Trace: samples=[] -> child_peak_rss = child_resource_peak (default), then line 261 guard fires only if child_resource_peak is not None, computing max(child_resource_peak, child_resource_peak) == child_resource_peak (no-op). samples=[500,300], child_resource_peak=None -> line 261 guard skipped, result 500. samples=[500], child_resource_peak=700 -> max(500)=500 then max(500,700)=700.
est_reduction: ~2 lines net; primarily a clarity improvement removing the overlapping default/max interaction.
behavior_preservation: Equivalent for all input combinations: empty/non-empty sample list crossed with None/int resource peak all yield identical results to the proposed single-aggregation form.
